newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SHANAHAN HAS SECOND HAT TRICK IN ROW AS WINGS ROUT SHARKS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SHANAHAN HAS SECOND HAT TRICK IN ROW AS WINGS ROUT SHARKS.

text.p: Brendan Shanahan scored three straight goals in the second period to become the first Red Wing to post hat tricks in consecutive games in nearly 18 years as Detroit routed the San Jose Sharks 7-1 Wednesday.
Shanahan, who scored three goals less than seven minutes apart, got his 10th career hat trick.

He added an assist on Detroit's first tally and, following Saturday's three-goal performance against Pittsburgh, became the first Red Wing since Vaclav Nedomansky in 1979 to accomplish the feat in consecutive contests.
"You could have put a hula-hoop around the spots that I scored from," Shanahan said. "After one period we were only up by one and we wanted to go out there and take them out of the game."
Shanahan has nine goals and two assists in his last six games.
Vladimir Konstantinov had two goals and two assists for Detroit, which improved to 19-2-1 against San Jose, including 11-0 at home.
"We could have had eight goals and we had a couple of others that could have gone in," Red Wings coach Scott Bowman said.
Detroit goaltender Chris Osgood made 27 saves in improving to 16-10-6.
After Chris Tancill scored for San Jose with 86 seconds left in the second period, Konstantinov, Sergei Fedorov and Tomas Sandstrom sealed the victory with third-period tallies.

In Pittsburgh, Niklas Andersson and rookie Jason Holland scored second-period goals and Tommy Salo made 29 saves as the New York Islanders surprised the Penguins 5-1, snapping a three-game winless streak.
Travis Green and Zigmund Palffy each added a goal and an assist for New York, which also halted a four-game road losing streak and won for just the second time in its last eight games overall.
Ron Francis had the lone goal for Pittsburgh, which has lost two in a row following a three-game winning streak.
In Edmonton, Rem Murray put home his own rebound with 4:58 to go in regulation to give the Oilers their seventh win in eight games, 4-3 over the slumping Boston Bruins.
Ryan Smyth and Miroslav Satan scored power-play goals in a 77-second span late in the second period for the Oilers. Todd Marchant also scored.
Ray Bourque, Tim Sweeney and Ted Donato tallied for Boston, which is winless in its last five games (0-4-1) and fell to 0-2 on its seven-game road trip.
In Buffalo, Vladimir Malakhov and Martin Rucinsky stayed hot with second-period goals and Jocelyn Thibault turned aside 32 shots but the Montreal Canadiens settled for a 2-2 tie with the Sabres.
Malakhov has four goals in six games. Rucinsky has eight goals and four assists in his last eight games.
The Sabres, playing without All-Star goaltender Dominik Hasek, got goals from Donald Audette and Jason Dawe and extended their unbeaten streak to eight games.
Steve Shields, filling in as an emergency replacement for Hasek, stopped 43 shots. Hasek returned to his native Czech Republic following the death of his father-in-law.

At Florida, Robert Svehla and Radek Dvorak scored on the power play in a three-goal third period and the Panthers extended their unbeaten streak to five games with a 5-2 victory over the Tampa Bay Lightning.
Martin Straka also tallied in the third period for the Panthers, who improved to 2-0-1 against their intrastate rivals this season and lead the all-time series, 11-4-3.
The Panthers played without injured regulars Ray Sheppard, Dave Lowry, Mike Hough, Brian Skrudland and Ed Jovanovski.
In Hartford, Dave Andreychuk scored off his own rebound with 3:44 remaining and the New Jersey Devils edged the Whalers 3-2, extending their unbeaten streak to a season-high eight games.
Denis Pederson scored twice and Randy McKay set up all three goals for the Devils, who are 4-0-4 in their streak. New Jersey has allowed only 15 goals during its streak.
In Anaheim, Roman Oksiuta, Jari Kurri and Paul Kariya each contributed a goal and an assist and Guy Hebert made 39 saves, helping the Mighty Ducks defeat the Toronto Maple Leafs 5-2.
The Ducks won for just the second time in six games but improved to 5-1 in their last six at home.
Doug Gilmour and Sergei Berezin tallied for Toronto.
In Dallas, Nikolai Khabibulin recorded his third shutout in 19 days and Darrin Shannon scored twice, leading the Phoenix Coyotes to their third win in four games, a 5-0 blanking of the Stars.
Mike Gartner added a goal and two assists for the Coyotes, who avenged Saturday's 5-4 overtime loss to Dallas, a game in which they squandered a 4-0 lead.
